notes: TBox revision, migrated 2026-11-11. The origin of a sea stack (cut out of a headland or cliff by the waves) is swapped for an earthquake, which is clearly false. Relation formed_by. Derivability very_unlikely: the definition is stated directly and follows from no other fact. No real exceptions: Wikipedia defines a stack as formed by wave erosion; its note that steep oceanic islets of volcanic origin are "loosely referred to" as stacks concerns volcanic remnants that the waves then cut, none raised by an earthquake. Audit fixes: three models answered the direct question 'Erosion' and were scored wrong against 'wave erosion', so the direct, Chinese and Spanish gold answers are now 'erosion' (the Spanish prompt said '¿Qué forma...?', which also reads as 'what shape', and now asks for the natural process). The edit is now worded 'formed by an earthquake' (was 'pushed up from the sea floor by an earthquake'), parallel to the original, so the propositional questions read more simply; three models had answered the old conjunction 'Yes'. The Cliffs of Moher side fact was replaced by a better-known one. Derived queries (inheritance, 2 hops, membership in the prompt): Am Buachaille and the Old Man of Stoer (kept) and the Duncansby Stacks, Scottish stacks known as landmarks or climbs but never written with their origin. The background-belief queries on the Twelve Apostles and the Old Man of Hoy and their worlds were dropped: TBox records now carry only determinate queries. Near unrelated: the state of a famous group of stacks (the Twelve Apostles, Victoria); its reference differs from the new answer. Every bridge is stated in its prompt, so only the propositional side facts need checks.
